attack_technique: Endpoint Denial of Service: Service Exhaustion Flood
description: Adversaries may target resource-intensive features of web applications to cause a denial of service (DoS). The HULK (HTTP Unbearable Load King) tool achieves this by randomizing HTTP headers and URI parameters for every single request. This forces the server to bypass lightweight caching mechanisms and exhaust heavy backend application processing resources (CPU/RAM).

patterns.description: Characteristics related to the manipulation of HTTP requests designed to bypass server defenses and target application logic.

features.name: Cache Bypass via Randomization
features.description: Every HTTP GET request features uniquely randomized headers, particularly the 'User-Agent' and 'Referer' fields, along with obfuscated URL parameters. This forces the application to dynamically generate every response.

features.name: Uniform Packet Structure (Low Variance)
features.description: Despite the randomized strings inside the headers, the overall mathematical variance of the packet lengths (Low Packet Length Variance) remains low across the flow, hinting at an automated script.

patterns.description: Anomalies related to the sheer volume and direction of the generated traffic.

features.name: High Forward Request Rate
features.description: A massive and sustained volume of packets pushed from the attacking client to the target server (High Flow Pkts/s and High Fwd Pkts/s) aimed at overwhelming the application layer.

features.name: Server Response Starvation
features.description: As the backend application becomes overwhelmed by processing complex requests, its ability to respond drops significantly, leading to a drastically reduced rate of return traffic (Low Bwd Pkts/s) and tiny response segments.

patterns.description: Timing behaviors associated with the attack's execution.

features.name: Erratic Inter-Arrival Times
features.description: The attack may exhibit unusually high maximum intervals between forward packets (High Fwd IAT Max) or elevated mean intervals (High Flow IAT Mean), often an artifact of the tool generating new randomized payloads on the fly.

patterns.description: Contextual indicators for distinguishing the attack from legitimate complex traffic.

features.name: Signature Evasion
features.description: Because the payload and headers change with every request, standard signature-based IDS/IPS systems fail to recognize a repeating pattern, requiring application-layer anomaly detection.

features.name: Legitimate Traffic Resemblance (False Positive Filtering)
features.description: The traffic volume and unique request patterns can sometimes mimic legitimate flash crowds interacting with an unoptimized search feature, or aggressive web crawlers.
